doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: European appreciation of art
summary: Europeans live for art; he thinks the US is improving, citing applause at Mostly Mozart.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Do you think jazz over there has a little bit of the — I don’t know if exotic is the right word — but the fact that it came from somewhere else gives it a little more juice.

Whether they appreciate it more because of that. No their appreciation for jazz is just like their appreciation for all art forms. They live for art. This is so important for them, to go to a concert. They will pass up a meal to go to a concert. They’ve been developed that over many years, that whole appreciation for art. They treat artists over there — they would have given Charlie Parker a city over there. They tried to get him to stay. They would have given him whatever he wanted. So it’s appreciation for art that they have. They’ll go 500 miles to hear a concert.
Well maybe because most of those countries are a lot older than the United States.
They’re real old. Yeah, they’re definitely old.
It’s taken all that time. So we’ll look to the future.
The States is doing pretty good, the United States is doing pretty good with their appreciation of art now too. I was watching television the other night and they had on the
Mostly Mozart series at Lincoln Center, and the guy was playing piano, he was playing really great too. And the people in the audience, they were smiling and they were applauding after each part.
They were applauding after each part of the composition. They don’t usually do that.
They’re supposed to wait ‘till the end.
